CITI BANK 
INTERVIEW EXPERIENCE (INTERNSHIP) 
 
 
HARSHIL SHAH 
TY - CS 
 
 
Timeline 
1) PPT – 6th September 
2) Online Test – 11th September 
3) Technical Interview – 14th September 
4) HR interview – 14th September 
 
 
 
PPT 
The PPT was very conclusive and detailed. They explained everything about Citibank and 
what it does. They explained the paper pattern and the platform on which the test 
would be conducted. Do attend the PPT as if you get selected you may have to face some 
HR questions which require the knowledge about the company and you won’t prefer to 
have that last minute hustle searching over for it on Google. 
 
 
Online Test 
 
Test was conducted on AMCAT platform. Test consisted of 5 sections. There were 
sectional timers. You cannot switch between sections. Also you cannot navigate 
through the questions within a section. There was no negative marking. 
General tip: Be real quick while solving questions! 
 
1. CS subjects’ based MCQs (25 Questions in 35 minutes) 
MCQs based on stacks, queues, trees, searching, sorting techniques, output 
prediction,basic programming questions,OOPS etc

Your basics should be really clear and you will be through this section. 
 
2. Aptitude (16 Questions in 16 minutes) 
MCQs on topics like work and time, probability, permutations and combinations, 
percentages, ages, proﬁt and loss, etc. I don't remember exactly what the 
questions were, but they were doable. The only thing is you need to be fast. 
3. Logical Reasoning (14 Questions in 14 minutes) 
 
I don’t clearly remember the questions of this section. But the questions were of 
easy to moderate level. 
4. Verbal Reasoning (22 Questions in 18 minutes) 
 
Antonyms, synonyms, prepositions and passages etc. The questions were easy. 
 
Tip: There were two passages. Each passage had around 3-4 questions. So 
reading the passage carefully once helps a lot. 
5. Coding section (2 Questions in 60 minutes) 
a. Trapezium Pattern Printing 
 
Question link - https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/program-to-print-the-trapezium-
pattern/ 
 
 
Passed 11/11 test cases 
b. Question was related to tree data structure 
(I don’t remember the question ) , Passed 2/13 test cases 
76 students were shortlisted for the interviews

Technical Interview 
 
Duration: 20 minutes (on zoom) 
All technical rounds started from 9.30. My interview was scheduled at 10. The interviewer 
was really friendly and he began the interview by introducing himself. Then he asked 
“Tell me about yourself” 
He looked quite impressed with my introduction. Then he asked me what is oops. After that 
he asked me to implement queue followed by adding and printing first 10 numbers in queue. I was 
asked to share my screen and code it in vs code. I was able to answer this question. Then he asked 
about what is a balanced Binary Tree and how can we make a binary tree balanced. I was able to 
answer this question (just explanation was required and not the code) 
After that he asked about what is an algorithm and what is the time complexity of two algorithm 
doing the same function. Then I told him that code of algorithm is required to calculate the time 
complexity and I explained him by giving examples. He seemed satisfied with the answer. Then 
he asked if I had any questions. (Do ask questions which will make interviewer feel you are 
interested) And the interview ended. 
 
I was selected for the next round along with 31 students

HR + Technical Round  
Duration: 30 minutes (on zoom) 
Tip: Be conﬁdent and be yourself! 
My interview was conducted at 12. It started with tell me about yourself.  Then he asked 
me about my projects . Why did you made this project. Which tech stack did you use. 
Was it a group or individual project, as I said it was an individual project then he asked 
why you made it individually and not in a group.  
 
After that he asked why do you want to join Citi. 
After that he asked if you have any questions? 
(Ask 1-2 questions so interviewer feels you are interested) And then the interview ended. 
 
 Finally 15 students were shortlisted for the internship and I was one of them!

Advice: 
Okay! So ﬁrst of all breathe. Take a deep breath right now. You must have read a lot of 
interview experiences and I can imagine how it feels. 
1) Always read company archives on gfg(and practice questions company wise as 
well) 
2) Give mock interviews as well (on interviewbit) 
3) Be well versed with your projects. I used the STAR(Situation, Task, Action, 
Result) approach to explain my projects. 
4) Prepare for the HR interview as well. It is always better to be prepared with the 
most commonly asked HR questions. 
5) There may be times when you will feel dejected, you will feel nervous, anxiety 
hogi bohottt but trust me the universe always sends the best. Even if it gets 
difﬁcult to have faith in yourself, convince yourself that you are gonna do this! 
6) Internship sab kuch nahi hota hai! (don't be harsh on yourself, but work hard) 
7) It's never too late to begin, never! Just chaalu kardo 
8) Optimism, meditation and the power of visualization are the best weapons to 
counter fear, nervousness and anxiety 
9) It is never about knowing everything and answering each question in an 
interview, it's always about how conﬁdently you handle situations where the 
question is unknown 
10) Always explain your logic and make very sure that you have completely 
understood what the interviewer is asking, speak out loud, tell the interviewer 
your approach and then code. 
11) Don't get confused: there are tons of resources available online, stick to a few 
only 
 
I know all of this is too much, but trust me, I have been there, have faith in yourself 
and bas karte jaao! Next year you will be writing about your interview experience for 
sure! 
 
 
All the very best
